subject: Request: temporary uptime waiver & remedy calculation for batched inference ramp
messages:
From: Tom Bowers <tom@edgewave.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ramp: SLA expectations and temporary exception request

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the batching improvements. We're preparing to ramp traffic for the EdgeWave pilot next week and I wanted to surface a couple of ask items from procurement/security before we go live.

Key point: during an aggressive ramp of batched inference we expect a short window where tail latency and transient availability could deviate from your standard template. Procurement is asking whether Redwood can accept a temporary adjustment to the uptime SLA for the first 60 days of the pilot, with a clear monthly remedy calculation so finance can forecast credits.

Specifically:
- Temporary uptime floor of 99.5% (vs standard 99.95%) for a defined 60-day ramp window.
- Remedy expressed as monthly service credit with a hard cap (EdgeWave prefers a 25% cap of the monthly commitment).
- We also need the latency p95 SLO for the batched endpoint and a trigger for latency-based credits (we'll provide a sample query distribution in the attached workbook).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited waiver and provide the credit formula (minutes-down -> credit percentage -> dollar credit) so our procurement/legal can sign off quickly? We're hoping to avoid lengthy redlines.

Attachments: EdgeWave_Pilot_Specs.xlsx (traffic profile)

Best,
Tom
Tom Bowers
Head of Platform Ops, EdgeWave Solutions
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bowers <tom@edgewave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ramp: SLA expectations and temporary exception request

Tom — thanks for the clear note and the traffic workbook. We're keen to support a smooth pilot ramp and avoid surprises on both sides. High level answers below; Ben/Laura I've looped you in for final approval on the numbers and legal language.

Short answer: we can offer a timeboxed waiver with explicit guardrails. Proposed structure:
- Standard hosted SLA remains 99.95% uptime.
- For the pilot ramp window (first 60 calendar days after go-live) we can accept a temporary floor of 99.5% for the affected batched endpoint(s).
- Remedy: monthly service credit calculated pro-rata on downtime minutes for the affected endpoint, with a per-month cap at 30% of the monthly committed spend (we're proposing 30% as a negotiation starting point). Formula we use internally (example):
  - downtime_minutes = cumulative minutes where availability < threshold for the endpoint in the month
  - raw_credit_pct = downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month * 100
  - applied_credit_pct = min(raw_credit_pct, cap_pct)
  - dollar_credit = applied_credit_pct / 100 * monthly_commitment

We can also define a latency credit trigger: where p95 latency for the batched endpoint exceeds 1.5x baseline for > 60 minutes in a calendar month, we apply a fixed 5% credit (adjustable).

We put together a redline of the SLA template that includes the pilot waiver and a sample credit calculation — attached SLA_Template_Redline_v1.pdf. A couple of operational notes:
- Maintenance carveouts will be limited to scheduled windows we agree to in advance; unplanned maintenance affecting availability will still count toward the calculation unless classified as emergency support (and then we'll document).
- We'll set a 30-day notice to terminate the waiver early (mutual agreement).

Ben/Laura — would you accept 30% cap and the latency-trigger approach, or prefer Tom's proposed 25% cap?

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ramp: SLA expectations and temporary exception request

Agree with Olga's approach but want tighter bounds on the credit math and an explicit sunset. My recommended edits:
- Cap: 25% of monthly commitment (EdgeWave asked for this; it's acceptable and keeps our downside limited).
- Month definition: use calendar month for calculations.
- Credit formula (concrete):
  - total_minutes_in_month = 30 * 24 * 60 (use actual calendar minutes where applicable)
  - downtime_minutes = cumulative minutes of endpoint unavailability measured by our monitoring (we should reference the exact metric id)
  - raw_credit_pct = min((downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) * 100, 100)
  - applied_credit_pct = min(raw_credit_pct, 25)
  - dollar_credit = applied_credit_pct / 100 * monthly_commitment
- Latency credit: make it sliding: for p95 degradation windows > 60 minutes we apply 2% credit per 60-minute block up to the 25% cap (so helps align to duration).
- Waiver duration: 60 days from go-live with automatic expiry; any extension requires written agreement.

Also flag to Legal: we'll need a short amendment (one-page) rather than a full SLA rewrite — please prepare language that references the SLA template and inserts the pilot clause.

I'll approve going to the customer with the 25% cap and sliding latency credit if Legal can turn the amendment quickly.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Bowers <tom@edgewave.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ramp: SLA expectations and temporary exception request

Olga, Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the concrete formula. EdgeWave is comfortable with the 60-day timebox and the 25% monthly cap. The sliding latency credit for p95 degradation also seems fair; we'll provide the baseline p95 numbers in the next hour so you can bake them into the monitoring alert.

Next steps for us:
- Please send the one-page pilot amendment we can sign (DocuSign link preferred).
- We'll finalize the traffic workbook and deliver the baseline p95 values by EOD.
- Agree to go-live Wednesday 2026-07-15 pending DocuSign.

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to a smooth ramp.

Best,
Tom Bowers
Head of Platform Ops, EdgeWave Solutions
Attachments referenced: SLA_Template_Redline_v1.pdf, EdgeWave_Pilot_Specs.xlsx
